sample_unit: survey respondents (medical students, house officers, residents, physicians, faculty)

links.outcome: Self-reported verification of AI outputs before use and awareness of fabricated references
links.effect: 59.2% (95% CI 54.2-64.1%) typically did not verify AI outputs; 40.2% had never heard AI can fabricate references; 36.5% assumed convincing AI references were authentic; 54.2% would keep using remaining content after finding one fabricated reference.
links.quote: Despite high adoption, 59.2% (95% CI: 54.2-64.1%) typically did not verify AI outputs before use, and 40.2% had never heard that AI can generate fabricated references.

links.outcome: Consistency of disclosure of AI use in research, by formal research training
links.effect: Consistent disclosure was 51.7% with formal research training vs 17.1% without (chi-square(1)=48.43, p<0.001, Cramer's V=0.36), indicating inconsistent disclosure overall.
links.quote: Formal research training was strongly associated with consistent disclosure (51.7% vs. 17.1%; χ²(1) = 48.43, p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.36).

unlisted_practices: Integrating AI literacy into medical curricula to improve verification and hallucination awareness

screen.reason: This is an empirical cross-sectional survey examining AI adoption, hallucination awareness, and verification/disclosure behaviors among medical trainees and professionals in Pakistan.
